title: Kernel switch regression playback — flash / pagedKV / continuous-batching (Mar 2025)
content:
Summary:
This note documents an exploratory regression observed after flipping kernel/runtime options in the staging serving cluster on 2025-03-11. The change simultaneously enabled flash attention, paged-KV (paged-kv), and continuous batching heuristics for a subset of models used in model-onboarding evals. We saw subtle but repeatable quality degradations on several prompt sets (mainly long-form summarization and multi-turn chat), with different fingerprints across kernels.

Objectives:
- Capture playback artifacts and metric diffs for the three runtime features enabled together.
- Provide per-prompt-set examples of quality regressions and possible root causes.
- Propose a short triage plan and a plan for gate tests to prevent regressions on onboarding.

High-level timeline:
- 2025-03-11 02:10 UTC: Canary hosts updated with runtime v1.18.3, flags: flash-attn=on, paged-kv=on, cont-batch=heuristic.
- 2025-03-11 03:30 UTC: Automated onboarding evals run (suite v2.4.1) across 6 models; anomaly alerts for tldr-suite and conv-quality suite.
- 2025-03-11 04:00 UTC: SRE rollback to runtime v1.18.2 on Canary; anomalies persist in canary replay (indicative of cached model artifacts).
- 2025-03-12 09:00 UTC: Replayed with paged-kv=off, flash-attn=on, cont-batch=off to isolate. Differences reduced but not eliminated for some prompts.
- 2025-03-13 15:00 UTC: Full artifact capture and manual inspection (this doc).

Scope / Affected workloads:
- Models: rwi-small-v1 (7B), rwi-medium-v2 (13B), rwi-chat-light (13B-chat).
- Prompt sets with regressions: longform-summarization-v1 (avg tokens 1200), multi-turn-product-support (avg history length 12 turns), prompt-compression-eval (prefix-heavy).
- Not affected (or no measurable regression): short-chat-bench, code-complete-bench.

Evaluation methodology (replay + metrics):
- All evals run against identical seeds and input streams using the playback harness (replay-id: playback-2025-03-11-01).
- Metrics collected: ROUGE-L, BLEU (where applicable), embedding-similarity (cosine on sentence-transformer), token-logprob delta, hallucination-count (human-labeled subset), latency p50/p95, throughput (tokens/sec), and KV cache hit-rate diagnostics.
- Differential reports computed between baseline (v1.18.2, flash=off, paged-kv=off, cont-batch=off) and three experimental permutations.

Key metric diffs (representative):
- Longform summarization (longform-summarization-v1) on rwi-medium-v2:
  - Baseline ROUGE-L: 32.8 -> Experiment (all on): 29.6 (relative -9.8%)
  - Embedding sim: 0.725 -> 0.684 (-5.6%)
  - Avg p95 latency: 340ms -> 220ms (improvement)
  - Token-logprob mean delta: -0.48 -> -0.62 (more negative; poorer fluency scores)
content_continued:
- Multi-turn product support (rwi-chat-light):
  - Baseline human hallucination count: 6/120 -> Experiment (all on): 18/120 (×3)
  - Coherence rating (0-5): 4.3 -> 3.8
  - Observed repetition behaviors in turn 7+: increased token duplication and cut-off mid-sentence.

Isolation experiments (short notes):
- flash-attn=on only (paged-kv & cont-batch off): minor quality delta; ROUGE-L down by ~1.5% on longform, hallucinations stable. Latency gains similar.
- paged-kv=on only: larger quality delta on long context prompts where prefix tokens > 8k (for models with large KV snapshots). Embedding similarity drops and occasional context truncation symptoms observed.
- cont-batch=heuristic only: rare token alignment issues in multi-turn chat (staggered KV read/write), but alone did not recreate the full regression.
- Conclusion: the biggest single impact on quality is paged-kv when combined with continuous batching heuristics; flash-attn amplifies small distributional shifts.

Repro examples (prompt + baseline vs experiment output snippets):
- Prompt (longform-summarization-v1, doc id 4938): "Summarize the following 1,200-word product design doc focusing on goals, constraints, and proposed experiments."
  - Baseline (snippet): "Key goals: reduce onboarding latency by 60%, maintain safety guardrails for user data. Proposed experiments: A/B test batching heuristics and cache warmup; success metric: 95th percentile latency under 400ms."
  - Experiment (snippet): "Goals include reduce onboarding, metrics... experiments: add batched heuristics... 95% success 400ms."
  - Notes: Experiment output shows dropped specifics (exact percentages), collapsed numeric details, and a generic phrasing that loses the technical nuance.

- Prompt (multi-turn-product-support, convo id 77): Scenario where user references earlier message asking account id; baseline maintains reference, experiment makes up a short ID that was never provided.
  - Baseline: "I see your account id ends with -A3F. I can link the ticket to that account."
  - Experiment: "I can link the ticket to account -A3F. Would you like me to proceed?" (fabricated confirmation and slightly different phrasing).

Hypotheses (ordered by likeliness):
1) Paged-KV page boundaries + continuous batching reorders some KV reads/writes under contention leading to stale/partial context visible to the decoder for long prompts. This would manifest as lost numeric tokens and hallucinated fillers.
2) Flash-attn kernel numerical differences (reduced precision fast path) amplify probability mass shifts in low-probability tokens (numbers, entities), making the model less likely to reproduce exact strings.
3) Batching heuristics change microtiming of KV swaps which alter attention window alignment for certain token positions (off-by-one-ish effects).

Evidence for hypothesis 1:
- KV page read logs for a failing replay show requests where page X is read twice with different base offsets; alignment delta correlates with positions where numbers were dropped.
- When paged-kv disabled, those misalignments disappear.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Are some model weight quantization profiles more fragile to flash-attn numeric paths? Need cross-model compare.
- Is the batching heuristic triggering different code-path when input size distribution skews? (We saw more regression when multiple long requests were pipelined).
- How often does this occur in production traffic (not just canonical evals)? We need a sample of prod traces.

Immediate remediation steps (short-term):
- Rollback plan already executed for canaries on 2025-03-11, but staging still showed artifacts due to cached KV state. Full staging restart with runtime v1.18.2 recommended. Owner: SRE (Marco).
- Add a temporary gating rule on model-onboarding suite: require no ROUGE-L degradation > 3% and hallucination count increase < 50% for any kernel change. Owner: Aisha.
- Add a playback test that replays mixed long and short request patterns to catch batching-edge cases. Owner: Jin.

Medium-term engineering actions:
- Add deterministic KV page alignment assertions in the paged-kv dev harness; fail-fast when page offsets mismatch. Owner: Ravi.
- Run numeric-sensitivity sweep for flash-attn vs standard attention on quantized vs full-precision builds (PR: runtime/pull/915). Owner: Applied-ML research.
- Improve logging to include per-request KV page lineage (trace id -> page reads/writes). Owner: platform-engineering.

Proposed onboarding gate/tests:
- Synthetic long-context suite with injected numeric tokens (IDs, percentages) and exact-match scoring for critical tokens.
- Mixed-latency concurrency test: 50% short, 50% long requests with cont-batch heuristics active; assert no >2% increase in hallucinations.
- Per-model sensitivity report to be generated when onboarding: baseline vs flash-attn vs paged-kv vs cont-batch permutations.

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Attach raw diff CSVs from replay (where available) to Confluence page. (TODO: Jin).
- Schedule a short triage sync with runtime infra and SRE to review page alignment logs (target: 2025-03-16).
- Decide whether to land the numeric-sensitivity sweep before the next staging rollout.

Appendix (quick links):
- Playback id: playback-2025-03-11-01
- Sample failing input ids: [4938, 5013, 5021, 5217] (these are internal eval ids — see Confluence page).
- Related PRs / diffs: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/915 (flash-attn default paths), github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/337 (paged-kv patch), jira://JIRA-ENG-4127 (incident ticket).
